events.title: Renaissance paintings by Antonello da Messina stolen from Sicilian museum
events.summary:
Theft of four works on national holiday described as wound to historical memory and cultural identity of city of Messina

Four of the most important works of art by the 15th-century Renaissance master Antonello da Messina were stolen during a national holiday from a museum in the Sicilian port city of Messina.

Thieves gained access to the Regional Museum of Messina, or MuMe, on Saturday evening, possibly capitalising on attention being focused on La Vara, a huge religious festival that takes place in the city on 15 August, when Italy marks the Ferragosto national holiday.

Continue reading...

events.title: Jared Kushner meets with Hamas ahead of talks with Netanyahu on Gaza
events.summary:
Trump’s son-in-law and envoy held rare meeting with Hamas chief in Egypt in push for progress on ceasefire

Donald Trump’s son-in-law and envoy, Jared Kushner, held a rare meeting with Hamas’s political chief on Sunday in Egypt, in a new diplomatic effort to make progress in the stalled Gaza ceasefire. Kushner will meet on Monday with Benjamin Netanyahu, who is under pressure after rejecting the new 15-point, US-backed road map.

The talks aim to salvage the plan for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw from the Palestinian territory shattered by war.

Continue reading...

events.title: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon kill 11 in worst toll since June truce
events.summary:
Rescue services search for survivors and bodies after airstrikes hit homes in Ansar and Deir al-Zahrani

Eleven people have been killed, including three children, and 19 injured in two Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon, the worst toll since deals in June brought a lull in hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah.

Israeli warplanes bombed a home on the outskirts of the village of Ansar, killing seven people and flattening the building early on Saturday morning. Rescue services were working at the site to try to find survivors and locate bodies.

Continue reading...

events.title: Trump threatens to declare strait of Hormuz ‘territory of the United States’
events.summary:
Seriousness of remark made in New York on Friday, and whether it signaled new policy ​position, not clear

Donald Trump has threatened to declare the strait of Hormuz as “a territory of the United States” as his administration struggles to conclude the war with Iran.

During a speech at a police academy on Long Island, New York, on Friday, the US president said he would “pretty soon” designate the waterway – a crucial chokepoint for global trade, through which about a fifth of the world’s seaborne oil supplies typically pass – a US territory.

Continue reading...

events.title: Israeli military plans to transfer law enforcement in occupied West Bank to police
events.summary:
Palestine’s vice-president calls plan ‘flagrant violation of international law’ and a step towards full Israeli annexation

Israel’s defence minister wants to transfer law enforcement powers for Israelis in the occupied West Bank over to the police, a plan that Palestine’s vice-president described as a “flagrant violation of international law” and step towards full Israeli annexation.

Israel Katz announced that he had ordered the military to draw up plans for the handover of responsibility for policing Israeli settlers amid domestic and international criticism of the army’s failure to tackle militants besieging three Palestinian families.

Continue reading...

events.title: Benjamin Netanyahu describes UK as ‘first Islamic republic to get a nuclear weapon’
events.summary:
Israeli PM criticised by political rival for attacking an international ally and overseeing ‘horrific diplomatic failure’

The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, called the UK “the Islamic republic of Britain” in a podcast interview, where he also described the country as the “first Islamic republic to get a nuclear weapon”.

His comments, made during an interview for Israel’s army radio, played into a common far-right Islamophobic trope about Britain’s small Muslim population.

Continue reading...

events.title: Taliban threaten former Afghan police worker after MoD leak reveals identity
events.summary:
UK has refused resettlement application despite ‘years of loyal service’ that have resulted in ‘constant fear’ of reprisals

A man has received threats from the Taliban after his work for the Afghan police was revealed by a Ministry of Defence leak and the UK refused his application for resettlement.

Hamid* worked for the Afghan national police special unit and received certificates for his work signed by senior British figures praising his “dedication, unparalleled service and leadership”. His details were also included in an accidental 2022 leak by an MoD official that identified 18,700 Afghans who had worked with or for the British government.

Continue reading...

events.title: Concerns grow over increased global ties with Taliban in Afghanistan
events.summary:
Campaigners fear deeper diplomatic contacts are undermining demands for improvements in human rights

The Taliban in Afghanistan have launched a diplomatic effort to end their isolation as major regional and international powers show a readiness to engage more closely with the repressive regime despite its systematic human rights abuses.

Five years after the Taliban took power, an increasing number of countries are renewing ties or scaling up diplomatic contacts with the hardline Islamists, who seized power in Kabul in 2021 after 20 years of brutal insurgent warfare.

Continue reading...

events.title: Ex-Myanmar ambassador to UK on trial for trespassing in diplomatic residence
events.summary:
Kyaw Zwar Minn was ousted for declaring loyalty to Aung San Suu Kyi after 2021 coup but refused to leave his home

Myanmar’s ousted ambassador to the UK has gone on trial on trespassing charges for refusing to leave a diplomatic residence after being unceremoniously locked out of the embassy in 2021.

Shortly after Myanmar’s military seized power in 2021, triggering mass protests that spiralled into a civil war, Kyaw Zwar Minn was locked out of the embassy for declaring his loyalty to the deposed civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

Continue reading...

events.title: The return of the caspian tiger: how a species feared extinct has come back to Kazakhstan
events.summary:
The wild capture and release of a female big cat into a nature reserve is the first step towards reintroducing a population that hasn’t been seen for 70 years

On 31 July, “Umit” – which means hope in Kazakh – was released into a nature reserve on the edge of Lake Balkhash after more than a decade of careful planning to return the caspian tiger to the region. With this release, Kazakhstan became the first country to restore its tiger range after they had been thought extinct, with the last reliable sighting in the country recorded more than 70 years ago.

Umit – a wild-caught female tiger transported from the Russian far east – will be joined by more big cats in the coming years, with plans to establish a self-sustaining population of about 50. A wild-caught male flown from Russia is still being monitored by authorities and will be released when he is judged fit to survive alone. Two wild tiger cubs are also being reared on the reserve in special enclosures, with as little human contact as possible, and are likely to be released into the marshlands next year, to feast on boar, deer and kulans, a type of wild donkey.

Continue reading...

events.title: As conflict in the Middle East intensifies, India’s relationship with Israel deepens
events.summary:
An Amnesty International report reveals that the country is now a key part of Israel’s weapons supply chain. Plus, Assam floods, student anger spreads and a song to put in rotation

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Hello, and welcome back to This Is India.

For this week’s newsletter, I’m looking at India’s evolving relationship with Israel, and how it has deepened as conflict swept across the Middle East. Why is it that India has formed an even closer bond with a country that has faced mounting international isolation and backlash over a military campaign in Gaza that has left the territory in ruins and killed more than 70,000 Palestinians, – many of whom were children?

Continue reading...

events.title: Reform accused of targeting the most vulnerable with £50bn benefit cut
events.summary:
Robert Jenrick takes aim at disabled people and foreign nationals after saying UK guilty of ‘suicidal empathy’

Reform UK has been accused of excluding the most vulnerable from society and punishing non-Britons living in the UK as it prepared to outline £50bn of cuts to benefits for disabled people and foreign nationals.

Robert Jenrick, Reform’s finance spokesperson, will detail the plans for £20bn of cuts to disability benefits overall, as well as another £21bn from stopping foreign nationals – including EU citizens with settled status – claiming almost any benefits, among other cuts.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘It’s been very tough’: hope of progress in gruelling battle against south Wales wildfire
events.summary:
Efforts of emergency services and military in Blaenavon appear to be working but there are fears for the future

More than three weeks after it began burning and two days after the military deployed to the area, there is hope that the huge wildfire on the hillside above the Ebbw valley village of Blaenavon may finally be coming under control.

Emergency workers and soldiers described a gruelling battle against the deep-seated peat fire that has spread over 4,000 hectares (9,800 acres), putting lives, farmland and property at risk.

Continue reading...

events.title: Water companies in England and Wales explore ‘surge pricing’ during drought
events.summary:
Suppliers could factor water scarcity into charges as part of Ofwat proposal to reduce consumption

Water companies could be allowed to raise bills for customers during periods of drought under proposals being considered by the sector’s regulator for England and Wales.

Suppliers would be permitted to factor “water scarcity” into bills as part of efforts to reduce consumption under Ofwat’s plans, which are being likened to surge pricing – the practice where private hire firms raise taxi fares at times of higher demand.

Continue reading...

events.title: Arron Banks hired private investigators to dig into Conservative party chair
events.summary:
Revelation comes after it was disclosed that Reform UK backer had paid for spying on prominent journalist

The businessman and Reform UK backer Arron Banks commissioned a private intelligence firm to dig into the Conservative party chair, in addition to having paid for an investigation into a prominent journalist.

Banks, a former Reform UK candidate and leave campaign donor, appeared to confirm on Sunday that he was behind an investigation into Kevin Hollinrake.

Continue reading...

events.title: Cambridge University defends its mental health support for Jason Arday
events.summary:
University says it continued to provide support after resignation of academic, who was found dead on Friday

The University of Cambridge has defended its mental health support for the academic Jason Arday.

The university said it had continued to provide Arday with extensive mental health support and security measures, including installing panic alarms and screening racist emails and post, after he resigned from his post as professor of sociology of education this month.

Continue reading...

events.title: Lala weakens to tropical storm as it lashes Hawaii with heavy wind and rain
events.summary:
Hurricane Lala downgraded after skirting Big Island as one person dies and more than 200,000 homes and businesses without power

Hurricane Lala weakened to a tropical storm on Sunday after skirting Hawaii without making landfall, but it wasn’t done punishing the Big Island with hurricane-force gusts. Total rainfall of nearly 3ft (1 meter) was expected on the higher windward slopes, turning rivers into raging torrents and threatening mudslides.

The Hawaii governor, Josh Green, said at least one person died in a car accident in the South Point area of the Big Island, where more than 100 homes were destroyed. More than 200,000 homes and businesses were without power on Sunday afternoon across Hawaii’s three largest islands, according to the utility tracker PowerOutage.us. At least three hospitals were operating on generator power, and 19 roofs were lost, Green said.

Continue reading...

events.title: Republican senator denounces Trump’s ‘crazy, stupid’ claims about MMR vaccine safety
events.summary:
Outgoing Louisiana senator Bill Cassidy, a medical doctor, voted to confirm anti-vaccine activist RFK Jr as health secretary before speaking out

Republican senator Bill Cassidy – a medical doctor who voted to confirm anti-vaccine activist Robert F Kennedy as federal health secretary in early 2025 – on Sunday denounced Donald Trump’s “crazy, stupid” claims about the safety of the combined MMR vaccine for undermining faith in immunization.

When Trump recently ordered changes to the recommended childhood vaccination schedule, with Kennedy by his side, the president called for two shots of the combined Measles, Mumps and Rubella vaccine to be scrapped in favor of two doses of three separate vaccines, claiming that the MMR shots are “sort of like a nuclear weapon” that could be “quite lethal”.

Continue reading...

events.title: Suspect in Virginia State University shooting found hiding in dorm closet
events.summary:
Suspect, 19, who is not enrolled at the university arrested in connection with shooting of five people, authorities say

A young man suspected in connection with the shooting of five people on Saturday on the campus of Virginia State University (VSU) hid in a dormitory closet for more than 14 hours before being found and arrested, according to authorities.

The suspect – identified as 19-year-old Camron Harris – was found in Seward Hall on VSU’s campus at 4pm, local police Lt James Lamb said, according to the Virginia news outlet WTVR. The shooting occurred at about 1.30am on Saturday.

Continue reading...

events.title: At least six people dead from days of storms and record flooding in Indiana
events.summary:
Four-year-old boy, two men and three women among those who died since storms began on 11 August, officials say

Days of storms and flooding in Indiana left at least six people dead as flood waters peaked in Indianapolis’s White River – and rains were expected to ease in the state capital region and other parts of the state on Sunday.

A four-year-old boy, two men and three women were among those who had died since the storms began on 11 August, state homeland security department spokesperson Liz Woods said.

Continue reading...

events.title: Democrats demand answers from Trump on USS Abraham Lincoln conditions
events.summary:
Senator Ruben Gallego calls carrier’s months-long deployment a ‘deep problem’ as wellbeing concerns mount

Democrats on Sunday intensified their demands for answers from the Trump administration over conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln as the aircraft carrier’s nearly nine-month deployment continued fueling concern over crew morale, mental health and living conditions.

Ruben Gallego, a Democratic senator from Arizona, said on Sunday that problems aboard the Lincoln had kept mounting – and he blamed the carrier’s prolonged deployment on the unresolved war that Donald Trump started in February with Iran as well as lackluster leadership in general from the Republican president’s administration.

Continue reading...

events.summary: Lebanon's prime minister denounced the attacks on villages in southern Lebanon for targeting civilians in their homes. Israel said it was firing on Hezbollah infrastructure.

events.summary: Climate action does not seem to be a priority for the German government — despite record temperatures, heat-related deaths and drought. Why aren't more people taking to the streets in protest?

events.summary: A hurricane is forecast to hit the Big Island of Hawaii this weekend, bringing heavy rain and wind. Should it make landfall, Lala would be the first hurricane to hit the island since 1871.

events.summary: Russia is constructing high-rises in the occupied Ukrainian city of Mariupol, on the sites of buildings it destroyed. Who's buying these properties? And what happened to the Ukrainians who used to lived here?

events.summary: After the Taliban retook power on August 15, 2021, Berlin promised to bring Afghan staff to Germany. But people are still waiting to leave in Pakistan and Afghanistan.

events.title: Trump's Latin America allies open arms to Israel
events.summary: While ongoing military actions in Gaza and settler attacks on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank have largely isolated Israel globally, Latin America's authoritarian right sees an opening for a strategic alliance.

events.title: India: Modi promises free exam coaching, AI training for youth after protests
events.summary: Speaking on India's Independence Day, PM Modi announced free online coaching for competitive exams and AI training for 10 million youths, weeks after protests over alleged exam paper leaks and recruitment irregularities.

events.title: Germany: Evacuated villagers return after Eifel wildfire eases
events.summary: Most residents evacuated from the village of Gey have returned home after firefighters brought a major wildfire in Germany's Eifel region largely under control. DW has more.

events.title: Jason Arday: Ex-Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism scandal found dead
events.summary: Jason Arday, the youngest ever Black professor at Cambridge, was found unresponsive at an address in London. Arday had recently resigned in the midst of a plagiarism row.

events.title: Germany: Firefighters say Eifel wildfire now under control
events.summary: Firefighters in Germany say they have gained the upper hand in a fire that blazed for days in the Hürtgen Forest. More than 2,000 residents were forced from their homes by the flames and smoke.

events.title: Can a giant Madonna help slow secularization in Poland?
events.summary: Europe's largest statue of the Virgin Mary will be inaugurated on Saturday in the Polish village of Konotopie. What will the monument mean for the village it towers over — and for the Catholic faith in Poland?

events.title: Berlin's Russian House: A hub for propaganda and espionage?
events.summary: The Russian House stands in the heart of Berlin. Critics have long said it's being used to spread propaganda for Putin's Russia. Now, French authorities have said it is being used by the Kremlin for espionage.

events.title: Why women are breaking men's endurance records
events.summary: Sophie Woods has completed the 2,000-kilometer Via Alpina faster even than the fastest-ever man. DW explains why she is not the only woman breaking men's records in extreme sports.

events.title: Hunger stones: The history behind 'if you see me, weep'
events.summary: Centuries-old hunger stones are emerging as Europe's rivers recede. Among the most famous is the Decin hunger stone in the Elbe River with its cryptic message.

events.title: Can a drug help prevent trauma? Study with mice suggests so
events.summary: Researchers in Munich and Stockholm blocked the lifelong social cost of early adversity in mice with a single compound. The catch: it only worked when given during the trauma, not after.

events.title: Romania shuts nuclear plant, Hungary dams dry Danube River
events.summary: Romania has shut down its only nuclear plant in a rare move prompted by the lack of cooling water from the Danube River. Hungary, meanwhile, is racing to dam the Danube, trying to keep its Paks plant online.

events.title: Ukraine's monthly civilian casualties highest since 2022
events.summary: UN monitors say civilian casualties in Ukraine hit their highest monthly level since the start of Russia's full-scale war. The latest attacks included a Russian drone strike on a train, killing two workers.

events.title: How Germany's drone defense fails
events.summary: Drone defense is a priority for the German government. The latest dramatic incident involving an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig airport shows there are still substantial shortcomings.

events.title: Does the clean energy transition need forever chemicals?

events.title: Why is Russia's Yabloko party barred from upcoming election?
events.summary: Russia's highest court has banned anti-war opposition party Yabloko from September's parliamentary election. What does this mean for the election campaign, opponents of the war and for the political mood in the country?

events.title: 25 years Ohrid Agreement: Is N. Macedonia's peace holding?
events.summary: A quarter of a century after the Ohrid Framework Agreement ended North Macedonia's 2001 conflict, analysts warn that peace between ethnic communities remains fragile.

events.title: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft
events.summary: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.

events.title: Unconstitutional? German intelligence to receive more powers
events.summary: German intelligence agencies have been calling for more powers in the fight against cyberattacks, terrorism and extremism. Now the government has given the go. Critics warn that red lines are being crossed.

events.title: Italy: Etna eruption in Sicily halts Catania flights
events.summary: Sicily's Catania airport has suspended flights again as Mount Etna continues to spew lava and volcanic ash. The eruption has disrupted travel during the peak summer holiday season.

events.title: Short on US Patriot missiles, Ukraine looks for alternatives
events.summary: Russia is putting pressure on Ukraine with ballistic missiles, but Kyiv is short of Patriot interceptors. Domestic production and European alternatives take time. Can Kyiv realistically reduce its dependence on the US?

events.title: Germany news: Cabinet approves intelligence service reforms
events.summary: Germany's domestic and foreign intelligence services are to get greater powers to deal with hybrid threats. Meanwhile, transport ministers are meeting to find solutions to increasingly low river levels.

events.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
events.summary: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.

events.title: AI helping create popular mobile sports games

events.title: Can Turkey's new PKK law bring peace?
events.summary: Turkey's parliament has passed a framework law for the peace process with the Kurdistan Workers' Party. What does it stipulate, why is it controversial and what does it mean for the future of the peace process?

events.title: Hungary's parliament elects Orban critic as new president
events.summary: Hungary's parliament has overwhelmingly confirmed Andras Baka, formerly the head of the Supreme Court, to the largely ceremonial role of president. New Prime Minister Peter Magyar controversially removed his predecessor.

events.title: Making sense of Trump's executive order on US vaccinations
events.summary: President Donald Trump and his Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long tried to reduce the number of vaccinations available to the US public and even farm animals. The latest move in context.

events.title: Bulgaria drone crash a wake-up call for country's defenses
events.summary: The explosion of a Ukrainian decoy drone in Bulgaria near the Romanian border reveals gaps in Bulgaria's defenses, raises questions and shines a light on the country's policy shift on the war in Ukraine.

events.title: Germany news: Some shipping stops as Rhine hits new lows
events.summary: The summer heat is not only causing water levels in Germany's key river arteries to drop to dangerously low levels, but also contributing to wildfires in several areas. Follow DW for more.

events.title: How one German city plans to challenge climate extremes
events.summary: Western Europe has recorded its hottest-ever June and July, and extreme weather from drought to storms is here to stay. How can we adapt to a fundamentally altered climate? Cities like Kiel are trying new ideas.

events.title: Turkey MPs back historic law on reintegrating PKK militants
events.summary: Turkey's parliament has taken a major step toward ending four decades of conflict with the PKK. The new law sets out how some militants can return to civilian life, but leaves Abdullah Ocalan's future unresolved.

events.title: How the Rhine drought threatens Germany's economic recovery
events.summary: Germany's inland waterways still move around 5% of the nation's goods. With the Rhine at a critically low level, DW explores how the drought is hitting the economy where it hurts most.

events.title: UEFA, other football federations unite against Infantino
events.summary: A few weeks ago, Gianni Infantino looked set for another unopposed term as FIFA president. Now, with an election looming, the beleagured football executive is counting the numbers and could be hanging by a thread.

events.title: When extreme heat threatens Europe's nuclear power
events.summary: Warm rivers and low water levels are forcing nuclear power plants to reduce output across Europe. Over a year, the losses are minimal, but on critical days the loss of power has consequences for grids and prices.

events.title: Type 2 diabetes in young women increasingly common
events.summary: British researchers say rates of type 2 diabetes are growing most among women under 40. The disease is often underdiagnosed in women or diagnosed too late to reverse the condition's progression.

events.title: Western Europe records hottest June and July on record
events.summary: Drought is gripping large parts of Europe, with soils unusually dry and major rivers running low. A strengthening El Nino could push global temperatures even higher later this year.

events.title: Germany news: Berlin to step up drone security research
events.summary: Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said Germany is moving to counter the threats posed by drones. Meanwhile, the transport minister said he wants Deutsche Bahn bonuses tied to punctuality targets.

events.title: Study: Obesity 'bigger cancer risk' than previously thought
events.summary: A new study has found that being significantly overweight could be responsible for more cases of cancer than previously known. Abdominal fat, in particular, increases the risk of cancer — especially among women.

events.title: FIFA warns against 'concerted effort' to undermine Gianni Infantino
events.summary: Pressure is mounting on the FIFA president Gianni Infantino after plans to sell a stake in the World Cup collapsed and fresh allegations emerged relating to his time at UEFA.

events.title: Germany: Interior Minister warns of 'daily' hybrid warfare
events.summary: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt says attacks by foreign powers have become a constant threat to Germany. His remarks come just days after an explosive-laden drone was found at Leipzig airport.

events.title: Kosovo PM Kurti egged in parliament amid political crisis
events.summary: Kosovo has held three elections in over two years. Albin Kurti's ruling Vetevendosje is struggling to garner the two-thirds majority required to elect a president.

events.title: When German Catholics and Protestants share a church
events.summary: Each year, dozens of churches are decommissioned, demolished or repurposed in Germany. But there is a new, unique development.

events.title: Germany debates reintroducing mandatory civilian service
events.summary: Social organizations are skeptical about the government's ideas for a civilian service program that youths could choose as an alternative should Germany reinstate mandatory military conscription.

events.title: Ceuta: Spain sets up border controls on travelers from Italy
events.summary: Spain had warned Italy it would impose entry checks on visitors unless Rome halts its controls by Sunday. Even though they don't share a land border, the countries entered a spat after the Ceuta border rush.

events.title: Iceland's EU vote: A nation divided over Europe
events.summary: Security concerns, control over fishing rights and rising living costs are shaping Iceland's debate over whether to restart talks on joining the European Union.

events.title: Eco wins: Hungary goes solar, marmots go viral and Rome gets an upgrade
events.summary: From Hungary's accidental solar revolution to marmot crowdfunding and a long-overdue upgrade for Rome's big snake, good news comes in strange packages this week.

events.title: Germany: Far-right AfD extends its lead in nationwide polls
events.summary: In the latest Sunday poll, the AfD continues to pull ahead. And more and more people are against excluding the right-wing populists from decision-making, at least on a case-by-case basis.

events.title: Testosterone and fertility: the trade-off men aren't told about
events.summary: Testosterone is trending in gyms, on social online and in politics. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth even wants troops screened for low testosterone. But taking supplements can shut down the body's natural production.

events.title: Drought threatens power supplies in Danube countries
events.summary: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.

events.title: Mata Hari: Celebrated dancer turns WWI spy
events.summary: Mata Hari enthralled Europe's elite with her beauty and performances. Accused of spying during World War I, she faced a French firing squad in 1917.

events.title: AfD threatens to cut funding for 'modern-thinking' culture
events.summary: The far-right party could win an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's state election in September. Their cultural program denigrates Bauhaus, Holocaust remembrance culture and diversity in theater.

events.title: Germany: Leipzig airport drone attack sets off alarm bells
events.summary: German authorities have begun a counterterrorism ⁠investigation into a drone laden with explosives found near a Ukrainian transport plane at Leipzig Airport. It is seen as a "hybrid attack scenario."

events.title: How Gianni Infantino rose to rule football
events.summary: Gianni Infantino is staying on as FIFA president despite growing pressure to step down. So who is football's most powerful man, why did UEFA and others turn against him, and how did he reassert his authority?

events.title: Germany: 10 years of 'Integration Act' for refugees
events.summary: The German Integration Act aimed to regulate the integration of recognized refugees following high levels of immigration, facilitating access to the labor market in return for integration efforts.

events.title: Why is Russia selling its gold?
events.summary: Russia has become one of the world's biggest sellers of gold over the past 12 months. It's an attempt to raise cash in the face of budget issues, but not necessarily a sign of a looming financial crisis.

events.title: Germany: Court jails far-right youth terror cell members
events.summary: A Hamburg court has handed down stiff prison sentences to members of the far-right terrorist group "Last Wave of Defense." Politicians are warning that those drawn into extremist violence are getting younger.

events.title: The hidden problem with small modular nuclear reactors
events.summary: Mini nuclear reactors are seen as a flexible energy source. Their promise: abundant energy, cheap, clean and climate-friendly with lower water use. But do the numbers add up? We look at what's behind the SMR hype.

events.title: My sleep deprivation is your natural short sleep
events.summary: Every so often we hear of high-ranking politicians or CEOs claiming to get by on very little sleep — some as little as three hours a night. If they're not natural short sleepers, chances are they're heading for trouble.

events.title: AI ecosystem's 'circular' investment: risk or advantage?
events.summary: Amid talk of an AI sector bubble, one aspect is under scrutiny. Many big AI players are invested in smaller ones, who then buy the bigger firm's products. This brings risks and advantages.

events.title: South Sudan: How climate change can result in toxic water
events.summary: Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.

events.title: Tennis star Sabalenka supports sport's new sex test policy
events.summary: The world number one women's tennis player supports the WTA's new sex testing rules. Others are more critical of the policy.

events.title: Germany news: Hedgehog triggers police alert
events.summary: Police responding to a supermarket burglar alarm in central Germany found it was caused by an unlikely culprit. Germany's flag carrier, Lufthansa, has turned in poor quarterly results. DW has more.

events.title: More cancer-prone? Why younger generations may be at risk
events.summary: Researchers are observing certain age-related types of cancer more frequently in younger people. A new study suggests this could be because younger generations are aging faster than their parents or grandparents.

events.title: Binging on cringe: It's as addictive as 'eating junk food'
events.summary: Flexing achievements? Cringe. Expressing genuine emotions? Cringe. You want to look away, but you can’t. Cringe. It's so addictive, people have built social media careers by monetizing other people's worst moments.

events.title: What happens next for Infantino and FIFA?
events.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino is under pressure after the failure of his plan to create a commercial subsidiary for the World Cup. But will he be ousted? And what is needed for that to happen?

events.title: Fact check: Russian disinformation targets German elections
events.summary: Ahead of four elections in Germany this fall, dozens of fake posts are circulating online aimed at discrediting candidates and portraying Germany as divided. Analysts warn that Russia is now targeting local candidates.

events.title: The economic toll of Spain's wildfires
events.summary: Devastating wildfires are ravaging Spain's tourism, economy and nature. Could the country have done more to prevent them?

events.title: Germany news: DB hampered by 'organized irresponsibility'
events.summary: DB chief Evelyn Palla wants to overcome the culture of ''organized irresponsibility" by empowering new decision-makers within the railway operator. Bavarian brass musicians have wrapped up a 72-hour concert. DW has more.

events.title: Germany: As temperatures rise, so does climate skepticism
events.summary: Some 98% of active climate scientists say climate change is happening, and is man-made. Nonetheless, a new study shows the number of climate-change skeptics in Germany has increased. Why is that?

events.title: More women die in heatwaves, but biology 'isn't main cause'
events.summary: In country after country, more women are dying from the heat than men. But researchers say biology isn't the main reason. Age, working conditions, and unequal access to rest may drive the gap.

events.title: What's really causing Europe's wildfires
events.summary: From Greece to France, Europe is burning. But what's the real reason for the historic blazes ripping through the continent and why are they getting harder to stop?

events.title: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
events.summary: From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

events.title: Humanoid robots: Trump's latest China trade battle?
events.summary: The US has banned foreign-made humanoid robots, a market Chinese tech firms dominate. Although Washington cited national security risks, analysts think Donald Trump is buying time for US robot makers to catch up.

events.title: Eco wins: From death strip to nature haven and other green surprises
events.summary: A Cold War relic becomes a biodiversity haven, a Pokemon Go for trees and seagrass gets a second life. This week's eco wins come from some unexpected places.

events.title: FIFA plans: Infantino under pressure as senior advisor quits
events.summary: After regional football federations condemned FIFA plans for private investment, Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, tendered his resignation.

events.title: German court rules that AI music firm Suno violated copyrights
events.summary: Germany's state-mandated licensing agency, GEMA, says the verdict has "global significance," as Suno is also directed to pay yet-to-be-quantified damages.

events.title: BMW to Volkswagen: How deep is Germany's auto industry cull?
events.summary: BMW joins VW, Porsche and Mercedes-Benz in cutting thousands of jobs, as Chinese rivals erode their market share. DW recaps the major reforms German automakers are pursuing to safeguard their future.

events.title: Why Germany may stand up against FIFA's World Cup sell-off
events.summary: Leading figures in German football have lined up to criticize Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell a stake in the World Cup. Germany is showing signs that they may be ready to oppose Infantino's re-election.

events.title: 'Rienzi': Why this Wagner opera is so relevant today
events.summary: The opera sparked controversy long before its Bayreuth Festival premiere, and the debate hasn't died down since it came to the stage. Now, another controversy surrounds the new AI-generated Ring cycle.

events.title: K-pop's BTS opt out of new Asian music Grammy consideration
events.summary: The K-pop sensation BTS, snubbed when nominated for Grammys in the past, say they're not interested in winning a new Asian music category.

events.title: World Cup sell-off: Has FIFA finally gone too far?
events.summary: A new FIFA proposal to sell off a stake in the World Cup has been met with fury in the football world. Under Gianni Infantino’s presidency, FIFA has become increasingly profit-driven, but is this too much?

events.title: Bayreuth Festival opens with celebration and commemoration
events.summary: To mark its 150th anniversary, the Bayreuth Festival remembers victims of the Holocaust — and confronts its founder's antisemitism.

events.title: How two wars and El Nino could fuel world hunger
events.summary: The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East haven't yet crippled global food supplies. Add a powerful weather pattern like El Nino, however, and the risks multiply.

events.title: Germany: How weather extremes impact local agriculture
events.summary: Heat, drought, heavy rain and late frosts are taking a toll on German farmers. They increasingly respond with adapted varieties, new crops, modern breeding techniques and modified farming methods.

events.title: FIFA plans to form new commercial subsidiary and sell stake
events.summary: FIFA has announced plans to form a commercial subsidiary and to sell a non-controlling interest to private investors. It needs approval from member associations, but is claiming that it will benefit them financially.

events.title: Why is Germany building roads for yesterday's climate?
events.summary: As the Autobahn buckles under heat waves, Germany is still paving roads for a past climate. Engineers know how to fix that — so what's the holdup?

events.title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern and WAFCON
events.summary: Bernadette Amani joined Bayern Munich in January and is now captaining Ivory Coast in their first WAFCON in 12 years. Getting to the top hasn't been a straight path for the newly crowned German double winner.

events.title: 'Loneliness influencers': Being alone brings in the clicks
events.summary: No friends, no dating, no problem? Many influencers are presenting social isolation as a lifestyle. But experts warn of the consequences.

events.title: As US-Iran war rages, who's risking the Strait of Hormuz?
events.summary: Though Iran continues to attack vessels as leverage in its war with the United States, data show that several shippers continue to transit the waterway.

events.title: 'Amnesia' about measles risk and low vaccination rates have helped US infections grow
events.summary: The latest US data show measles cases from January to mid-July 2026 totaled more than all cases in 2025. Experts blame a fall in vaccination and warn that people have forgotten measles can be life-threatening.

events.title: FIFA boss Infantino takes aim at World Cup critics
events.summary: In a strongly worded open statement, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has hit out at those he says were too "consumed by hate and criticism" to enjoy the tournament. Infantino brushed off a number of corruption concerns.

events.title: Car ramming attacks: Why do they keep happening?
events.summary: Cars are being used as weapons, to ram, kill and maim innocent people. The reasons why are not always clear, nor are solutions to preventing such attacks.

events.title: WAFCON 2026: What you need to know
events.summary: Several months after it was supposed to start and with more teams than first planned, WAFCON 2026 is finally set to begin. The hosts want a maiden title while a tournament outsider have one of its best players.

events.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
events.summary: Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

events.title: Tour de France final stage shortened due to wildfires
events.summary: Security personnel assigned to the race have been redeployed to help contain major blazes near Bordeaux, reducing Sunday's final stage.

events.title: Eco wins: Cities, creatures, and tech are saving the day
events.summary: From an AI-powered cute little pangolin, heat mapping to cool down cities and animals reducing wildfire risks by doing their thing, these real-world climate hacks are helping communities stay ahead of a changing planet.

events.title: Highs and lows as Bayreuth Festival turns 150
events.summary: The Bayreuth Festival's 150th anniversary has been clouded by controversy surrounding German-Jewish speaker Michel Friedman. Yet it offers an opportunity to celebrate, including with an AI-enhanced Ring cycle.

events.title: Why Trump's 'forced labor' tariffs leave the world puzzled
events.summary: After the US Supreme Court struck down Donald Trump's emergency tariffs, the White House has turned to another trade law linked to alleged human rights abuses.

events.title: The trees helping fires spread and what to do about it‌
events.summary: With Spain declaring an emergency, France seeking EU help and Canada dealing with more than 900 hot spots, wildfires are out of control. Monocultures and climate change are partly to blame but can we stop the burning?

events.title: How vanilla's history is not so … 'vanilla'
events.summary: Long before "vanilla" meant bland, the bean's fandom spanned Mesoamerican elites to European courts. But it owes its ubiquity to a 12-year-old enslaved boy.

events.title: Klopp named new head coach of Germany men's football team
events.summary: Germany has turned to Jürgen Klopp to lead a new era for the four-time world champions after their disappointing World Cup exit, with hopes of building toward future international tournaments.

events.title: Jürgen Klopp and Germany: A partnership long in the making
events.summary: In one of the worst-kept secrets in football, the former Dortmund and Liverpool boss has been named head coach of the German men's national team.

events.title: Spain's solar eclipse trilogy: Spectacle starts August 12
events.summary: From August 2026 to January 2028, amateur and pro sky watchers are in for a series of rare solar spectacles over Spain and North Africa. Astronomers expect the events to attract millions from around the world.

events.title: ECB keeps interest rates unchanged amid Iran war inflation
events.summary: The European Central Bank has kept its base interest rates steady but said it was "closely monitoring" the energy price shock. The impact of the war against Iran on energy costs has pushed inflation over ECB targets.

events.title: Oil prices jump as Hormuz, Red Sea crises deepen
events.summary: Renewed strikes on shipping in the Gulf and the Red Sea have dealt a fresh double blow to global oil markets, with the price of crude oil once again passing $100 a barrel. DW examines what could push prices even higher.

events.title: US citizens are ramping up pressure on data centers
events.summary: Rapid data center construction across the US, fueled by AI, comes with serious threats to the environment, public health and energy supply. Local opposition has blocked or delayed dozens of projects.

events.title: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
events.summary: China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

events.title: Female coaches want more representation in African football
events.summary: Female head coaches will be a rare sight at the Women’s African Cup of Nations. However, there are some promising signs.

events.title: Will surge in German business bankruptcies hit growth?
events.summary: Company insolvencies in Germany are rising sharply. Is this a sign of deeper economic weakness, or just a market correction that could ultimately benefit future growth?

events.title: Austria turns Hitler's birthplace into police station
events.summary: The house where Adolf Hitler was born in 1889 is now a police station. Austrian authorities have long sought to prevent it becoming a neo-Nazi pilgrimage site.

events.title: Can VR help you achieve your goals?
events.summary: A Max Planck researcher has developed VR and smartphone tools that let you "meet" your future self. The science behind it is more powerful than it sounds.

events.title: 'Antifa' song climbs to top of charts after TV show cancellation
events.summary: German rapper Danger Dan and pianist Igor Levit had been invited to play a song for the 100th episode of a political satire show on TV. The performance was canceled at the last minute due to its message.

events.title: Why the youth jobs crisis is becoming global
events.summary: Young people in much of the world face growing competition for entry-level jobs as graduate numbers rise, hiring slows and AI-driven disruption adds uncertainty to career prospects.

events.title: How heat waves are messing with your sleep
events.summary: Residents across Europe have struggled to sleep during the latest record heat waves. But as the planet continues to warm, sleep deprivation could create an epidemic of mental and physical ill-health.

events.title: England and Liverpool football legend Kevin Keegan dies aged 75
events.summary: English former striker and manager Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75 after a battle with cancer. He was a two-time European footballer of the year with Hamburg.

events.title: How 'blue dot fever' is affecting concerts
events.summary: Live music remains popular, but many concerts are struggling with unsold tickets and cancellations. While superstars fill stadiums, smaller venues and acts are facing a crisis.

events.title: Taking stock of 2026 World Cup: Football's biggest show yet
events.summary: A worthy world champion, a call from the US president, security concerns and a few pleasant surprises: The biggest World Cup ever is now over. So what will we remember about the 2026 World Cup?

events.title: 🔴 Cameroon beats Malawi to win Women’s Africa Cup of Nations for the first time
Cameroon beats Malawi to win Women’s Africa Cup of Nations for the first time
events.summary: Cameroon defeated tournament debutant Malawi in the final of the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations on Sunday, winning the trophy for the first time. The Indomitable Lionesses, who failed to qualify for the previous edition of the tournament, had lost on their last three appearances in the final – all to 10-time winner Nigeria.

events.title: Drone and missile strikes kill 19 in Russia and Ukraine
events.summary: At least 19 people were killed Sunday in drone and missile strikes in Russia and Ukraine which destroyed a book market in Kyiv while Moscow faced one of the most massive attacks since the start of the war. Ukraine and Russia have been escalating their long-range strikes for months, resulting in a growing number of civilian casualties, more than four years after the start of the Russian invasion.

events.title: French swimmer Léon Marchand wins gold in Euros 400m freestyle
French swimmer Léon Marchand wins gold in Euros 400m freestyle
events.summary: French swimming star Léon Marchand won the 400m freestyle final at the European swimming championships Sunday in Saint-Denis, near Paris.

events.title: Senegal: Saint-Louis’ centuries-old pirogue racing tradition
events.summary: In Saint-Louis, Senegal, traditional pirogue races are keeping alive a centuries-old tradition dating back nearly 200 years. Held in the fishing district of Guet Ndar, the 3.5-kilometre race brings together dozens of rowers and huge crowds, turning the event into both a major sporting competition and a celebration of local culture. But despite the race's popularity and the money it generates, competitors are not paid and are calling for greater recognition for the sport.

events.title: Italy: Four Renaissance artworks stolen from Messina museum in Sicily
events.summary: Four artworks by Renaissance painter Antonello da Messina have been stolen from the Museo Regionale in Messina, Sicily, overnight on August 15. The thieves took three panels from his Polittico di San Gregorio, depriving the city of part of the only surviving works by the painter still held in his hometown. Italian authorities have launched an investigation. FRANCE 24's Seema Gupta, correspondent in Italy, has the latest.

events.title: Iran offers $30,000 bounty for killing or capturing US soldiers
events.summary: The Iranian military announced on Sunday it would be offering a $30,000 reward for killing or capturing US soldiers, with the bounty doubled if conducted by a woman. There have been no known deployments of US ground troops in Iran during the war except for a rescue mission carried out in April.

events.title: India: Modi courts youth amid growing criticism
events.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi put young people at the heart of his development agenda in a speech marking India’s Independence Day on Saturday. He announced free online coaching for competitive exams and plans to train 10 million young people in artificial intelligence over the next year. The speech comes amid growing criticism of Modi’s Hindu nationalist policies and recent youth-led protests against his government, as analyzed by FRANCE 24's, Jamie Smith-Maillet.

events.title: Ukraine: Russian strike destroys Kyiv book market
events.summary: Kyiv was hit by Russian strikes on Sunday, killing at least four people and injuring six, while a popular outdoor book market was destroyed. Vendors rushed to the scene to assess the damage, with some saying they had lost their shops and their livelihoods.

events.title: West Bank: Activist recounts life under settler siege in Qusra
events.summary: A week after Israeli settlers began besieging Palestinian homes in the West Bank village of Qusra, human rights activist Netanael Hanadaro joined FRANCE 24 to recount what he witnessed there. He said he and other NGO members reached the isolated homes on foot and left food outside for the trapped residents, with the Israeli army saying it would deliver the supplies. Hanadaro described an extraordinary situation in which the homes, located on the outskirts of the village, have been surrounded by settlers while the army works to prevent clashes between the settlers and activists.

events.title: Death toll from Zimbabwe capsized ferry accident rises to 84
events.summary: Rescue workers recovered more bodies on Sunday following a ferry capsizing accident that occured earlier this week on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, bringing the death toll to at least 84. The search continues, as authorities fear the number of casualties could rise even further.

events.title: WAFCON final: Women's sport seeks greater recognition
events.summary: The Women's Africa Cup of Nations final takes place tonight in Rabat, with Malawi facing Cameroon in a historic showdown. Speaking to FRANCE 24, sports journalist Charlotte Richardson discussed the growing popularity of women's sport, but also the persistent gaps in media coverage, funding and infrastructure compared with men's competitions. She also highlighted the WAFCON's last-minute postponement earlier this year, saying such a decision would be unthinkable in men's football.

events.title: South Lebanon: How will Israeli strikes affect negotiations?
events.summary: Israel killed 11 people in strikes on southern Lebanon on Saturday, in what has been described as the biggest threat to the peace talks since the June agreement. Ziad Majed, Professor of Middle East Studies at the American University of Paris, spoke to FRANCE 24 about the potential impact of the strikes on the negotiations underway in Rome, the role of the United States, and Israel's policy towards Lebanon and especially Hezbollah.

events.title: Poland-registered bus veers off Hungary highway, killing 12 people
events.summary: A crash involving a bus registered in Poland killed 12 people and severely injured at least 10 early Sunday on a Hungary highway, marking the worst accident of its kind in the country in more than 20 years. Poland will send an emergency aircraft to Budapest, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced.

events.title: Week in pictures: A solar eclipse, quake in Colombia and Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank
events.summary: A solar eclipse seen across parts of Europe, ongoing search-and-rescue efforts in Colombia after a devastating earthquake killed at least 300 people and left hundreds missing, and escalating violence by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, condemned by the US ambassador to Israel as "acts of terror": FRANCE 24 takes a look at the week's most striking images.

events.title: Kushner, Hamas delegation in Egypt for talks on Gaza peace plan
events.summary: A Hamas delegation held talks with Egyptian intelligence chief Hassan Rashad in Egypt on Sunday, followed by talks with US envoy Jared Kushner. Kushner had met shortly before with President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in an effort to break the deadlock over the US-brockered peace plan for Gaza.

events.title: Brazil election: Lula and the new face of Bolsonaro's right
events.summary: Brazil's October presidential election is shaping up as another battle between the Lula and Bolsonaro camps, with incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva seeking a fourth term and Flávio Bolsonaro stepping in for his imprisoned father. The two frontrunners are running close in the polls, as Lula focuses on Brazil's sovereignty amid tensions with Washington, while Flávio leans on his family's far-right support and ties to Donald Trump.

events.title: France: Landes wildfire stopped spreading but remains out of control
events.summary: Firefighters in southwestern France are continuing to battle a wildfire that has burned 1,700 hectares of forest in the Landes region. The blaze has stopped spreading but remains out of control, with 550 firefighters, military personnel and six water-bombing aircraft working to contain it and allow evacuated residents to return home.

events.title: 🔴 Live: Ukraine launches 600 drones at Russia, one of its largest aerial attacks of the war
South Lebanon: Doctor describes escalating humanitarian toll
events.summary: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon have killed at least 11 people, in what local authorities describe as the largest escalation since the June agreement. Speaking to FRANCE 24, Pierre Catoire, an emergency doctor working in the area, described a deteriorating humanitarian situation, saying some doctors lost their homes in Saturday’s strikes and healthcare workers are increasingly worried that hospitals could also be targeted. He said the most common injuries are blast and compression wounds, while doctors are also concerned about infections, as well as the long-term psychological impact on civilians.

events.title: Chad : Opposition figure Succès Masra speaks to France 24
events.summary: Chadian opposition leader and former Prime Minister Succès Masra, who founded the opposition party Les Transformateurs and challenged President Mahamat Idriss Déby in the 2024 presidential election, was jailed for more than a year after being sentenced to 20 years in 2025. Pardoned by Déby on August 14, he has now spoken to France 24 about Chad's political situation and his future.

events.title: WAFCON: Malawi and Cameroon face off for historic first crown
events.summary: Malawi and Cameroon will face off this Sunday in Rabat at 9pm Paris time in the final of the Women's Africa Cup of Nations. A surprising matchup, with each nation hoping to secure the first continental title in its history.

events.title: Why France's under-15 social media ban was blocked
events.summary: France's attempt to ban social media for under-15s has been blocked by the Constitutional Council, which ruled the measure unconstitutional. Speaking to FRANCE 24, Peter Craddock, Senior Attorney advising social media companies, said the decision was unsurprising, arguing that the proposed law imposed a blanket ban without taking into account differences between platforms or children's levels of maturity. The court found that the measure infringed on the fundamental freedom of expression and information.

events.title: 'A wake-up call': Ebola outbreak is now DR Congo's deadliest
events.summary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has officially become the deadliest in the country's history, data suggests.

events.title: Five teenagers dead in car crash after vehicle driven wrong way on motorway
events.summary: Five male teenagers have died and more people are seriously injured after a crash on a motorway in County Kildare, Irish police have said.

events.title: Twelve killed as tourist bus crashes in Hungary
events.summary: Twelve people have been killed after a Polish tourist bus crashed in Hungary.

events.title: Two die in Spain mudslide as Belgium battles largest-ever wildfire
events.summary: Two women, aged 60 and 80, have been killed after torrential rain triggered a landslide in northwest Spain.

events.title: Cristiano Ronaldo says it is 'probably' his last season
events.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has said the new football season is "probably" his last.

events.title: Renaissance paintings stolen on Italian national holiday
events.summary: Four Renaissance paintings have been stolen from an Italian museum during the country's summer national holiday.

events.title: More than 100 arrested in Morocco after call for another migrant mass crossing to Ceuta
events.summary: At least 111 people have been arrested for trying to get into Ceuta following another call on social media for a mass crossing of migrants.

events.title: 'Fury' over death of teen British cyclist during Portugal race
events.summary: The cyclists' union is "filled with anger" after the death of British rider Finlay Tarling during the Volta a Portugal race.

events.title: More bodies found after ferry disaster in Zimbabwe as number of deaths climbs to 72
events.summary: Twenty-six more bodies have been found after a ferry capsized in Zimbabwe - taking the total number of deaths to at least 72.

events.title: Trump dismisses concerns about conditions on US aircraft carrier
events.summary: Donald Trump has downplayed the impact on American sailors who have spent nearly nine months at sea on the USS Abraham Lincoln.

events.summary: Authorities in Zimbabwe continue searching for bodies after an overloaded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba last week, killing more than 80 people

events.summary: Moroccan security forces have arrested hundreds of migrants trying to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta by land and sea

events.title: Kushner has a rare meeting with Hamas' leader on the Gaza road map. A meeting with Netanyahu is next
events.summary: U.S. negotiator Jared Kushner has held a rare meeting with the Hamas chief in Egypt in a push to make progress on the stalled Gaza ceasefire

events.title: Brazil's Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro return to their strongholds to kick off presidential campaigns
events.summary: Brazil's presidential candidates have kicked off their campaigns ahead of what is expected to be tight election in October

events.title: Colombian president asks Trump to suspend tariffs to help earthquake recovery
events.summary: Colombia's President Abelardo de la Espriella has asked U.S. President Donald Trump to suspend tariffs to help Colombia recover from a devastating earthquake

events.title: BBC asks a US court for help in getting testimony from the Trump family in defamation suit
events.summary: The BBC has asked a U.S. court for help getting documents and testimony from U.S. President Donald Trump's family in connection to his $10-billion defamation lawsuit against the broadcaster

events.title: Israel's Ben Gvir advocates killing '30 to 40' people in Gaza nightly while speaking to ex-hostage

events.summary: A magnitude-7.7 earthquake hit off the coast of Indonesia in the eastern Flores region, according to the United States Geological Survey. At least two people were killed and others injured.

events.title: Powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake causes intense shaking near Indonesia
events.summary: A magnitude-7.7 earthquake struck off Indonesia’s coast around 5 a.m. local time at a depth of about 6 miles, causing significant damage but not generating a major tsunami. NBC News meteorologist Bill Karins reports.

events.title: U.S. Ambassador Huckabee condemns ‘Israeli terrorists’ for siege of West Bank homes
events.summary: Dozens of Israeli settlers have trapped two Palestinian families in their West Bank homes for days, cutting off food, water and electricity. Their actions even drawing the ire of U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee. The IDF says settlers were dispersed, but some remain. NBC News' Matt Bradley reports from the occupied West Bank.

events.title: Once-in-a-lifetime total solar eclipse sweeps across Europe
events.summary: The moon passed directly in front of the sun Wednesday, briefly turning day into twilight as crowds from Iceland to Spain looked up in awe at the rare celestial spectacle. NBC News’ Gadi Schwartz reports.

events.title: Jason Arday, ex-Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism, found dead a week after resigning
events.summary: Former Cambridge professor Jason Arday was found dead at his London home on Friday, one week after he resigned from his position after accusations of plagiarism.

events.title: Magnitude-7.7 quake hits off coast of Indonesia, killing at least 47

events.title: ‘Revenge is inevitable’: Iran ramps up propaganda war with violent billboards
events.summary: Anti-U.S. messaging has intensified since the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, with artificial intelligence playing a major role.

events.title: ‘Tinderbox’ Britain bans disposable barbecues, sends nationwide fire alerts as Europe battles blazes
events.summary: LONDON — The U.K. imposed a temporary ban on the sale of disposable barbecues and sent a nationwide alert warning of a “very high risk of wildfires” as European countries battle to keep blazes under control.

events.title: More than 160 people killed in Colombia’s strongest earthquake in years
events.summary: At least 132 people were killed Monday in a 7.4-magnitude earthquake that shook western Colombia, collapsing hospitals, schools and other buildings and leaving people trapped under the rubble.
